label: Qualitative evidence synthesis protocol
framework: ENTREQ-informed qualitative evidence synthesis with GRADE-CERQual planning

items.prompt: What exact title should appear on the protocol?
items.helpText: Name the review type, topic, population or context, and main concept/intervention where relevant.
items.exampleResponse: Protocol for a scoping review of digital adherence technologies for tuberculosis treatment.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Protocol version and date.
items.prompt: What protocol version, date, registration status, or update status should be recorded?
items.helpText: Include version number, protocol date, registration plan or registry identifier, and amendment status.
items.exampleResponse: Version 1.0, dated 20 May 2026. Registration will be submitted before screening starts.

items.prompt: Who are the authors, contributors, affiliations, and corresponding contact?
items.helpText: List author names, institutional affiliations, contributor roles, and corresponding author details.
items.exampleResponse: Lead author: Evidence Synthesis Unit, Example University. Correspondence: lead@example.org.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Funding and competing interests.
items.prompt: What funding, sponsorship, and competing interest information should be declared?
items.helpText: State funder role, institutional support, conflicts of interest, and independence of the review team.
items.exampleResponse: This work is institutionally funded. The funder will not influence screening, synthesis, or conclusions.

items.requirement: Identify the document as a qualitative evidence synthesis protocol.
items.prompt: What is the title and qualitative synthesis focus?
items.helpText: Name the phenomenon, participants, and context.
items.exampleResponse: Qualitative evidence synthesis protocol: experiences of community health workers delivering hypertension care.

items.prompt: What topic, programme, condition, policy, or evidence problem is the protocol addressing?
items.helpText: Describe the practical or scientific issue that makes the review necessary.
items.exampleResponse: The review addresses uncertainty about how digital adherence technologies are being used in tuberculosis programmes.

items.requirement: Protocol element: What is already known.
items.prompt: What is currently known from existing literature, prior reviews, policy reports, or practice experience?
items.helpText: Summarize the current state of knowledge without writing the full review findings.
items.exampleResponse: Existing studies suggest promise, but evidence is scattered across programme reports, trials, and implementation studies.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Evidence gap or uncertainty.
items.prompt: What specific gap, uncertainty, inconsistency, or decision problem remains unresolved?
items.helpText: Identify what current evidence does not adequately answer and why that matters.
items.exampleResponse: Decision-makers lack a consolidated picture of which technologies have been evaluated, in which settings, and for which outcomes.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Why this review type.
items.prompt: Why is this specific review product the right method for the question?
items.helpText: Justify the chosen product, such as systematic review, scoping review, EGM, rapid review, realist review, or living review.
items.exampleResponse: A scoping review is appropriate because the evidence is heterogeneous and requires mapping before effectiveness questions are narrowed.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Decision and user context.
items.prompt: Who needs this protocol or review, and what decision or research use will it support?
items.helpText: Name the intended users, decision timeline, policy context, programme need, or research planning purpose.
items.exampleResponse: The synthesis will support programme planners deciding whether to commission a more focused effectiveness review.

items.requirement: Explain why qualitative synthesis is needed.
items.prompt: What experiences, meanings, barriers, facilitators, or implementation questions does this synthesis address?
items.helpText: Link the need to understanding acceptability, feasibility, equity, or implementation.
items.exampleResponse: Quantitative evidence shows mixed uptake; qualitative synthesis is needed to understand acceptability and implementation barriers.

items.prompt: What is the main review question in one clear sentence?
items.helpText: Write a question that matches the review type and can guide eligibility, extraction, and synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: What evidence exists on digital adherence technologies for tuberculosis treatment in low- and middle-income countries?

items.prompt: What are the framework elements for the question?
items.helpText: Define PICO, PCC, SPIDER, CMO, map dimensions, or another appropriate framework.
items.exampleResponse: Participants: people receiving TB treatment; Concept: digital adherence technologies; Context: low- and middle-income countries.

items.prompt: What is deliberately inside or outside the review question?
items.helpText: Clarify boundaries such as settings, populations, intervention forms, evidence types, or outcomes.
items.exampleResponse: The review will include patient-facing adherence tools but exclude provider-only electronic medical record systems.

items.requirement: State the review question using a qualitative question framework.
items.prompt: Define the SPIDER or PICo elements for the review question.
items.helpText: SPIDER can define sample, phenomenon of interest, design, evaluation, and research type.
items.exampleResponse: Sample: community health workers; Phenomenon: hypertension care delivery; Evaluation: perceived barriers and facilitators; Research type: qualitative studies.

items.prompt: What is the primary objective of the review?
items.helpText: State the main purpose using action verbs that match the review type.
items.exampleResponse: To map available evidence on digital adherence technologies for tuberculosis treatment.

items.prompt: What secondary objectives will the review address?
items.helpText: Include additional objectives such as identifying gaps, describing implementation, comparing evidence, or informing decisions.
items.exampleResponse: Secondary objectives include describing settings, evidence types, measured outcomes, and implementation barriers.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Planned use of findings.
items.prompt: How will the objectives connect to the intended use of the review?
items.helpText: Explain how the objectives will help users make decisions, design research, or interpret evidence.
items.exampleResponse: The findings will help identify where new evaluations or synthesis products are most needed.

items.requirement: State the review objectives clearly and in alignment with the review type.
items.prompt: What are the primary and secondary objectives this protocol will guide?
items.helpText: Objectives should match the review type: estimate, map, explain, synthesize experiences, compare reviews, or maintain living evidence. Frame objectives around experiences, meanings, barriers, facilitators, acceptability, feasibility, or implementation.
items.exampleResponse: The primary objective is to synthesize the available evidence for the defined question. Secondary objectives include identifying gaps and describing implications for decision-makers.

items.prompt: Which populations, participants, groups, or units will be eligible?
items.helpText: Specify age, condition, setting, role, location, or other defining characteristics.
items.exampleResponse: People receiving tuberculosis treatment, health workers supporting adherence, and programme implementers will be eligible.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Concept, intervention, or exposure.
items.prompt: Which concepts, interventions, exposures, policies, or programmes will be eligible?
items.helpText: Define the central thing being reviewed, including variants and exclusions.
items.exampleResponse: Eligible technologies include SMS reminders, digital pill boxes, video-observed therapy, and mobile adherence platforms.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Comparator, context, or setting.
items.prompt: Which comparators, contexts, settings, or geographic boundaries apply?
items.helpText: Use this element as needed depending on review type.
items.exampleResponse: Eligible settings include low- and middle-income countries; comparators may include usual care or alternative adherence support.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Outcomes, phenomena, or map domains.
items.prompt: Which outcomes, experiences, phenomena, or domains will be captured?
items.helpText: Name outcomes or phenomena that determine eligibility or extraction priorities.
items.exampleResponse: Domains include adherence, treatment completion, patient experience, implementation barriers, and equity considerations.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Evidence types and study designs.
items.prompt: Which evidence types, study designs, report types, or review products will be included or excluded?
items.helpText: State eligible designs and justify exclusions where needed.
items.exampleResponse: We will include empirical studies, programme reports, and systematic reviews with enough methodological detail.

items.prompt: What date, language, publication status, geography, or other limits will be applied?
items.helpText: Be explicit about pragmatic limits and their rationale.
items.exampleResponse: Records from 2010 onward will be included, with no language restrictions where translation is feasible.

items.requirement: Specify eligible qualitative and mixed-methods evidence.
items.prompt: Which qualitative designs, mixed-methods components, participants, contexts, and phenomena will be eligible?
items.helpText: Clarify how qualitative components of mixed-methods studies will be handled.
items.exampleResponse: We will include qualitative studies and extractable qualitative components of mixed-methods studies involving community health workers.

items.prompt: Which bibliographic databases will be searched?
items.helpText: List databases appropriate to the topic and review type.
items.exampleResponse: MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, Global Health, Scopus, and Web of Science will be searched.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Specialist sources and registers.
items.prompt: Which specialist databases, trial registers, review repositories, or evidence portals will be searched?
items.helpText: Include sources such as CENTRAL, Epistemonikos, PROSPERO, trial registries, Campbell, or 3ie where relevant.
items.exampleResponse: We will search Cochrane Library, Epistemonikos, trial registries, and relevant evidence portals.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Grey literature and websites.
items.prompt: Which grey literature sources, organisational websites, repositories, or policy sources will be searched?
items.helpText: List sources likely to hold reports, guidelines, theses, datasets, or programme documents.
items.exampleResponse: WHO, World Bank, ministry websites, NGO repositories, and institutional repositories will be searched.

items.prompt: What supplementary methods will be used to identify additional records?
items.helpText: Include citation chasing, reference list checks, expert contact, handsearching, or alerts.
items.exampleResponse: We will screen reference lists, conduct citation chasing, and contact topic experts for additional sources.

items.prompt: Which databases, repositories, registers, websites, expert sources, and grey literature sources will be searched?
items.helpText: Information sources should fit the review type and include enough coverage to reduce avoidable bias. Include databases and sources likely to identify qualitative studies and grey literature.
items.exampleResponse: We will search bibliographic databases, specialist registers, organizational repositories, relevant websites, and reference lists of included sources.

items.prompt: What core concepts and synonyms will structure the search strategy?
items.helpText: Break the search into concept blocks and note key synonyms.
items.exampleResponse: The search will combine tuberculosis terms, adherence terms, and digital technology terms.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Controlled vocabulary and keywords.
items.prompt: Which controlled vocabulary and free-text keywords will be used?
items.helpText: Mention MeSH, Emtree, CINAHL headings, or other index terms where relevant.
items.exampleResponse: Database-specific subject headings and free-text terms will be adapted for each source.

items.prompt: What search limits or restrictions will be applied and why?
items.helpText: Document date, language, geography, design, publication type, or source limits.
items.exampleResponse: Searches will be limited to records from 2010 onward because relevant digital tools emerged after that period.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Search peer review and documentation.
items.prompt: How will the search be reviewed, documented, and reproducible?
items.helpText: State who develops the strategy, whether it will be peer reviewed, and how full strategies will be stored.
items.exampleResponse: An information specialist will draft and peer review the search; full strategies will be included in an appendix.

items.prompt: Will searches be updated, monitored, or rerun before final reporting?
items.helpText: Describe planned search updates, alerts, or surveillance processes.
items.exampleResponse: The search will be rerun before final synthesis to capture newly published records.

items.requirement: Describe searches suitable for qualitative evidence.
items.prompt: Which databases, qualitative filters, citation searches, and grey literature sources will be used?
items.helpText: Qualitative evidence may require broad, sensitive searches and citation chasing.
items.exampleResponse: We will search MEDLINE, CINAHL, PsycINFO, Scopus, ProQuest, citation lists, and relevant institutional repositories.

items.prompt: What screening stages will be used?
items.helpText: Describe title/abstract screening, full-text screening, and any additional source classification stage.
items.exampleResponse: Records will undergo title/abstract screening followed by full-text eligibility assessment.

items.prompt: How many reviewers will screen records at each stage?
items.helpText: Specify independent, duplicate, single-reviewer, verification, or calibration methods.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will screen independently after piloting the eligibility criteria.

items.prompt: How will the team pilot or calibrate screening criteria?
items.helpText: Describe pilot sample size, calibration meetings, or criteria refinement.
items.exampleResponse: The team will pilot 50 records and refine guidance before full screening.

items.prompt: How will screening disagreements or uncertainty be resolved?
items.helpText: Specify consensus, adjudication, third reviewer, or stakeholder consultation.
items.exampleResponse: Disagreements will be resolved through discussion and, if needed, adjudication by a senior reviewer.

items.prompt: How will exclusion reasons and the selection flow be documented?
items.helpText: Describe full-text exclusion reasons and flow diagram reporting.
items.exampleResponse: Reasons for full-text exclusion will be recorded and summarized in a selection flow diagram.

items.prompt: How will records or sources be screened and selected, and how will disagreements or uncertainty be handled?
items.helpText: Specify screening stages, reviewer numbers, piloting or calibration, software, reasons for exclusion, and documentation. Clarify how qualitative and mixed-methods records will be screened for eligible qualitative data.
items.exampleResponse: Screening criteria will be piloted. Records will be screened at title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer.

items.prompt: What variables will be extracted or charted from each included source?
items.helpText: List bibliographic, methodological, population, setting, intervention, outcome, and finding fields as relevant.
items.exampleResponse: We will extract author, year, country, design, participants, intervention features, outcomes, findings, and limitations.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Extraction form and piloting.
items.prompt: How will the extraction or charting form be developed and piloted?
items.helpText: Describe draft fields, piloting, revisions, and final approval.
items.exampleResponse: The extraction form will be piloted on five included sources and refined before full use.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Reviewer process and verification.
items.prompt: Who will extract data and how will accuracy be checked?
items.helpText: Specify duplicate extraction, second-reviewer verification, or targeted checks.
items.exampleResponse: One reviewer will extract data and a second reviewer will verify key fields and all outcome data.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Handling missing or unclear data.
items.prompt: How will missing, unclear, or conflicting information be managed?
items.helpText: State whether authors will be contacted, assumptions recorded, or data marked as unclear.
items.exampleResponse: Missing information will be recorded as unclear; study authors may be contacted for priority missing data.

items.prompt: What tools and file structures will be used to manage extracted data?
items.helpText: Name spreadsheet, review software, coding software, or repository arrangements.
items.exampleResponse: Extracted data will be stored in a version-controlled spreadsheet with a data dictionary.

items.requirement: Describe extraction, coding, charting, or data transformation.
items.prompt: What data elements will be extracted or charted, and how will accuracy and consistency be checked?
items.helpText: Match the extraction fields to the review type and planned synthesis. Capture participant quotations, author interpretations, themes, context, and methodological features.
items.exampleResponse: A piloted form will capture bibliographic details, study characteristics, population/context, methods, findings, limitations, and fields needed for synthesis.

items.prompt: Will appraisal, risk of bias, quality, relevance, or rigour assessment be conducted?
items.helpText: State whether appraisal is required for this review type and how it will be used.
items.exampleResponse: Critical appraisal will be conducted to inform interpretation, not to exclude studies automatically.

items.prompt: Which appraisal, risk-of-bias, confidence, or rigour tools will be used?
items.helpText: Match tools to evidence type and design.
items.exampleResponse: Randomized trials will be appraised with RoB 2; qualitative studies with CASP; reviews with AMSTAR 2.

items.prompt: Who will conduct appraisal and how will disagreements be handled?
items.helpText: Specify reviewer numbers, calibration, consensus, and adjudication.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will appraise independently, resolving disagreements through consensus.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Use of appraisal in synthesis.
items.prompt: How will appraisal findings influence synthesis, confidence, or interpretation?
items.helpText: Clarify whether appraisal informs sensitivity analysis, weighting, confidence assessment, or narrative interpretation.
items.exampleResponse: Appraisal results will be reported in tables and considered when interpreting strength and credibility of findings.

items.prompt: Which qualitative appraisal tool will be used and how will appraisal influence synthesis?
items.helpText: Common tools include CASP, JBI qualitative appraisal, or MMAT for mixed-methods components.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will use the CASP qualitative checklist; appraisal will inform sensitivity analysis and confidence assessments.

items.prompt: What synthesis, mapping, integration, or theory-building approach will be used?
items.helpText: Name the planned approach and explain why it fits the question and data.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be synthesized narratively and organized by intervention type, setting, and outcome domain.

items.prompt: How will evidence be grouped, compared, or classified?
items.helpText: Describe planned categories, subgroups, map dimensions, themes, or theory configurations.
items.exampleResponse: Evidence will be grouped by population, technology type, setting, and measured outcome.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Quantitative synthesis or summary.
items.prompt: Will quantitative data be pooled, tabulated, or summarized descriptively?
items.helpText: State when meta-analysis is appropriate or why narrative/statistical summary will be used instead.
items.exampleResponse: Meta-analysis will be considered only where studies are sufficiently similar in design, intervention, and outcome.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Qualitative, conceptual, or explanatory synthesis.
items.prompt: How will qualitative findings, concepts, implementation factors, or explanations be synthesized?
items.helpText: Describe thematic synthesis, framework synthesis, realist synthesis, or another explanatory method where relevant.
items.exampleResponse: Qualitative findings will be coded into themes describing acceptability, feasibility, and implementation barriers.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Handling heterogeneity or variation.
items.prompt: How will heterogeneity, diversity, overlap, or contextual variation be handled?
items.helpText: Explain how variation affects synthesis, interpretation, or presentation.
items.exampleResponse: Variation by setting, population, intervention design, and evidence type will be explored narratively.

items.prompt: How will findings be presented to users?
items.helpText: Mention summary tables, evidence profiles, maps, joint displays, narrative summaries, or decision briefs.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be presented in structured tables, visual summaries, and a narrative synthesis organized around the review framework.

items.prompt: Which synthesis approach will be used, and how will findings be coded, compared, and developed?
items.helpText: Examples include thematic synthesis, meta-ethnography, framework synthesis, or best-fit framework synthesis.
items.exampleResponse: We will use thematic synthesis with line-by-line coding, descriptive themes, and analytical theme development.

items.prompt: Which certainty, confidence, or credibility framework will be used?
items.helpText: Name GRADE, GRADE-CERQual, AMSTAR confidence ratings, or a justified alternative.
items.exampleResponse: GRADE-CERQual will be used for qualitative findings, and review confidence will be reported for included reviews.

items.prompt: Which outcomes, findings, domains, or claims will receive certainty or confidence ratings?
items.helpText: Specify the unit of assessment.
items.exampleResponse: Confidence will be assessed for each major review finding and each priority outcome domain.

items.prompt: How will certainty or confidence judgments be reported and interpreted?
items.helpText: Describe evidence profiles, summary tables, ratings, and explanation notes.
items.exampleResponse: Confidence judgments will be reported with explanations for limitations, relevance, coherence, and adequacy.

items.requirement: Plan confidence assessment for qualitative findings.
items.prompt: Will GRADE-CERQual or another confidence approach be used for synthesized qualitative findings?
items.helpText: CERQual considers methodological limitations, coherence, adequacy, and relevance.
items.exampleResponse: We will use GRADE-CERQual to assess confidence in each review finding.

items.prompt: Which equity-relevant factors will be captured?
items.helpText: Consider place, race/ethnicity, occupation, gender, religion, education, socioeconomic status, disability, age, and other relevant factors.
items.exampleResponse: We will capture geography, socioeconomic context, gender, age, and health system setting where reported.

items.prompt: Which contextual or implementation factors may influence interpretation?
items.helpText: Capture health system, institutional, cultural, policy, implementation, or resource context.
items.exampleResponse: Implementation context will include service delivery setting, resource level, workforce model, and policy environment.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Subgroup or applicability plans.
items.prompt: Will the review assess subgroup differences or applicability to specific users?
items.helpText: State planned subgroup, applicability, transferability, or relevance considerations.
items.exampleResponse: Applicability will be considered by setting, population subgroup, and implementation intensity.

items.prompt: How will equity and context be reported in the final product?
items.helpText: Describe tables, narrative synthesis, map filters, or evidence profiles that preserve context.
items.exampleResponse: Equity and context data will be summarized in extraction tables and discussed in implications.

items.requirement: Describe equity, context, subgroup, and applicability considerations.
items.prompt: Which equity, context, setting, population, implementation, or applicability factors must be captured in the protocol?
items.helpText: Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting. Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting.
items.exampleResponse: We will extract and report context and equity-relevant characteristics, including setting, population subgroup, implementation environment, and applicability considerations.

items.prompt: Which stakeholders or evidence users will be involved?
items.helpText: Name policy, practice, community, clinical, methodological, or funder groups as relevant.
items.exampleResponse: Programme managers, community representatives, and evidence users will be invited to advise on scope and outputs.

items.prompt: At which stages will stakeholders be involved?
items.helpText: Specify input during question refinement, source identification, interpretation, dissemination, or product design.
items.exampleResponse: Stakeholders will be consulted during question refinement and interpretation of preliminary findings.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Use of stakeholder input.
items.prompt: How will stakeholder input be documented and used?
items.helpText: Explain how input changes scope, sources, interpretation, outputs, or priorities.
items.exampleResponse: Stakeholder feedback will be documented and used to refine categories, outputs, and dissemination messages.

items.requirement: Describe stakeholder engagement in question refinement, interpretation, or dissemination.
items.prompt: Which stakeholders will be involved, at what stages, and how will their input influence the review?
items.helpText: Stakeholders may help refine questions, identify sources, interpret findings, or shape outputs. Stakeholders may help refine questions, identify sources, interpret findings, or shape outputs.
items.exampleResponse: Stakeholders will be consulted during question refinement and interpretation of preliminary findings to improve relevance and usability.

items.prompt: What primary outputs will be produced?
items.helpText: Name manuscript, protocol registration, report, evidence map, data file, brief, or living update.
items.exampleResponse: Outputs will include a technical report, manuscript, and structured evidence tables.

items.prompt: Who are the audiences for each output?
items.helpText: Identify policy-makers, researchers, clinicians, communities, funders, programme teams, or guideline panels.
items.exampleResponse: Primary audiences include programme managers, guideline developers, funders, and research teams.

items.prompt: How will outputs be shared?
items.helpText: Mention journal publication, repository, website, presentation, webinar, policy brief, or stakeholder workshop.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be shared through a manuscript, policy brief, webinar, and institutional repository.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Open materials and data.
items.prompt: Will search strategies, datasets, codebooks, or appendices be made available?
items.helpText: State how supporting materials will be shared and any restrictions.
items.exampleResponse: Search strategies, extraction forms, and non-sensitive data will be shared as appendices or repository files.

items.requirement: Describe planned outputs and dissemination routes.
items.prompt: What outputs will be produced, who are the audiences, and how will findings be shared?
items.helpText: Consider manuscripts, briefs, map products, stakeholder reports, datasets, presentations, guideline inputs, and update notices. Consider manuscripts, briefs, map products, stakeholder reports, datasets, presentations, guideline inputs, and update notices.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be shared through a manuscript, technical report, decision brief, presentation, and accessible summary for stakeholders.

items.prompt: Which search strategies and source records will be appended?
items.helpText: Include database strategies, website search notes, dates, limits, and search logs.
items.exampleResponse: Appendix A will include full search strategies for each database and grey literature source.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Screening and extraction tools.
items.prompt: Which forms, templates, and coding tools will be appended?
items.helpText: Include eligibility criteria, screening form, extraction/charting form, codebook, and piloting notes.
items.exampleResponse: Appendix B will include the screening guide and extraction template.

items.requirement: Protocol element: Appraisal and confidence tools.
items.prompt: Which appraisal, risk-of-bias, or confidence tools will be appended?
items.helpText: Include adapted tools, decision rules, and scoring or judgment guidance.
items.exampleResponse: Appendix C will include appraisal tools and decision rules for confidence assessment.

items.prompt: How will amendments, deviations, and version history be documented?
items.helpText: Include an amendment log template with date, change, rationale, and approval.
items.exampleResponse: Appendix D will contain a dated protocol amendment and version history log.

items.requirement: Identify appendices required for transparency and reproducibility.
items.prompt: Which appendices will be included to document methods and decisions?
items.helpText: Appendices may include search strategies, screening forms, extraction forms, appraisal tools, coding frameworks, stakeholder materials, and amendment logs. Include coding framework, appraisal tool, extraction template, and CERQual evidence profiles if planned.
items.exampleResponse: Appendices will include database search strategies, screening forms, extraction templates, appraisal tools, coding framework, and protocol amendments.
